facts.F2: The appellant threatened Ms. Leung Sio Mei, Maria Rosa with injury to her property with intent to alarm her on 18 April 2009 at Luen Yan Street cooked food stall, Luen Yan Street in Tsuen Wan.
facts.F3: Ms. Maria Rosa Leung and her employee, Ms. Lin Wei, had each been employed by the appellant in a lunchbox business until their resignation on 9 April 2009.
facts.F4: After her resignation, Ms. Maria Rosa Leung set up her own business of providing lunchboxes for construction workers.
facts.F5: On 18 April 2009, the appellant appeared at Ms. Maria Rosa Leung's cooked food stall and asked her if she was taking away his lunchboxes.
facts.F6: The appellant pointed his finger at Ms. Maria Rosa Leung and said, 'Don't take away my lunchboxes again. If you take away my lunchboxes again, I will burn your vehicle down.'
facts.F7: Ms. Maria Rosa Leung was scared and made a report to the police that afternoon.
facts.F8: Ms. Maria Rosa Leung and Ms. Lin had a possible motive to fabricate their evidence against the appellant as a competitor in their new business.

reference_issues: Whether the magistrate erred in accepting Ms. Maria Rosa Leung as an honest and reliable witness.

Whether the magistrate erred in law in stating that the absence of testimony from the appellant left him without any explanation to undermine, contradict or explain the prosecution evidence against him.

Whether the magistrate erred in law in stating that if he disbelieved either Ms. Maria Rosa Leung or Ms. Lin on any material issue, he should exercise caution and be slow in accepting their evidence on any other material issues.
Whether the magistrate erred in stating that he was not 'impressed' by the evidence of Mr. Cheung.
authorities: Section 24(a)(i) of the Crimes Ordinance, Cap.200
relevant_cases:
Li Defan v HKSAR (2002) 5 HKCFAR 320
Chou Shih Bin v HKSAR (2005) 8 HKCFAR 70

claim: claims the Defendants are liable for Louvet's wrongdoing and/or knowingly assisting Louvet's fraud, also claims the Defendants were negligent or were in breach of their fiduciary duties towards the Plaintiff
requested_remedy: claims the Defendants are liable for Louvet's wrongdoing and/or knowingly assisting Louvet's fraud, also claims the Defendants were negligent or were in breach of their fiduciary duties towards the Plaintiff
parties: Defendant: FPB Asia Limited and First Pacific Bank Limited

facts.F1: Between 1987 and 1988, the Plaintiff remitted more than US$400,000 to the Defendants on the suggestion of Louvet to an account with IBI Asia Limited.
facts.F2: In August 1987, the Plaintiff drew a cheque for Swiss Franc 300,000 and sent it to Louvet at the Far East Bank, which was converted into Hong Kong dollars by Far East Bank Ltd and paid into an account of Modern China Development Ltd.
facts.F3: In 1988, Louvet fraudulently and dishonestly misapplied the Plaintiff's fund to settle the debt of Modern China Development owed to the Defendants.
facts.F4: The Plaintiff claims Louvet was dealing with the Plaintiff's money as his representative under powers of attorney granted by the Plaintiff to Louvet in his personal capacity and not as an officer of the Defendants.
facts.F5: There were substantial interlocutory applications including appeals since the commencement of the action.
facts.F6: In January 1997, the Plaintiff's solicitors indicated the need to re-amend the Statement of Claim, which the Defendants initially objected to.
facts.F7: The Defendants did not serve their Re-Amended Defence until 5 months after the Plaintiff indicated their wish to re-amend the Statement of Claim.
facts.F8: The Plaintiff had to take out a summons for specific discovery of relevant documents in June 1998.
facts.F9: A consent order was made allowing the Defendants to make discovery, but the Defendants did not comply.
facts.F10: The Defendants filed a further supplemental list of documents in November 1998, which led to exchanges of correspondence and requests for documents and inspections lasting for months until April 1999.
facts.F11: The Plaintiff consulted American lawyers on the powers of attorney in question.
facts.F12: The Plaintiff considered re-amendment to the Statement of Claim.

lawsuit_type: appeal against the order dismissing the Plaintiff's claim for want of prosecution
reference_issues: The relationship between the Plaintiff and Louvet at the material times and the circumstances in which the Plaintiff's monies were deposited with the Defendants through Louvet.
Whether the Plaintiff had expressly or impliedly authorised Louvet to execute the transactions in question, which transactions ultimately resulted in the Plaintiff losing all his monies.
Whether the Defendants had been negligent and/or were in breach of their fiduciary duties towards the Plaintiff.

claim: The Appellant was charged with 6 offences in the Magistrate’s court, including 4 counts of Indecent Assault and 2 counts of Common Assault.
requested_remedy: The Appellant was charged with 6 offences in the Magistrate’s court, including 4 counts of Indecent Assault and 2 counts of Common Assault.

facts.F1: The Appellant was charged with 6 offences in the Magistrate’s court, including 4 counts of Indecent Assault and 2 counts of Common Assault.
facts.F2: The offences were committed in a row between mid June 2003 and 29 June 2003.
facts.F3: PW1, a 19-year-old Indonesian domestic helper, worked for the defendant’s family from 12 January 2003 until mid June 2003.
facts.F4: PW1 alleged that the defendant indecently assaulted her on four occasions and hit her on two occasions.
facts.F5: The defendant denied all allegations, stating that PW1 was wearing jeans on the days in question, which could not be easily pulled down.
facts.F6: The defendant also claimed that PW1 made false accusations against him because she was unhappy with her work environment and wanted to terminate her contract.
facts.F7: The learned Magistrate convicted the defendant of all six charges and sentenced him to a total of 1 year’s imprisonment.
facts.F8: The defendant appealed against the conviction and sentence.
facts.F9: PW1 was considered by the learned Magistrate to be an honest and reliable witness.
facts.F10: The defendant’s evidence was considered to be not true and unreasonable.
facts.F11: The court considered the sentencing guidelines for cases of indecent assault, including the need to deter others, mark public abhorrence, and redress the grievance suffered by the victim.
facts.F12: The aggravating factors in this case include the victim’s age, the breach of trust by the defendant, and the lack of remorse shown by the defendant.

reference_issues: Whether the learned Magistrate erred in assessing the credibility and reliability of the witnesses, particularly PW1 and the defendant.
Whether the learned Magistrate erred in convicting the defendant of the six charges.
Whether the sentence imposed by the learned Magistrate was manifestly excessive.
relevant_cases:
HKSAR v. Cheung Kwai Sang
HKSAR v Chan Ching-ho [2001] 3 HKLRD 476

requested_remedy: arrears of rents, service charges and rates due and payable up to 10 December 2002 by the 1st Defendant as the tenant and by the 2nd Defendant as the guarantor, as well as for damages for breach of the Lease arising from the premature termination of the Lease
parties: Defendant: SUREX CONSULTANTS LIMITED, TANG MAN LUNG

facts.F1: The Plaintiff and the 1st Defendant entered into a lease agreement for the premises at Room 1207, 12/F., Harcourt House, 39 Gloucester Road, Wanchai, Hong Kong for a term of two years commencing from 16 July 2001 to 15 July 2003 at a monthly rent of $36,869 payable in advance on the first day of each and every successive calendar month.
facts.F2: The 1st Defendant failed to pay to the Plaintiff rent since 1 May 2002, services charges since 1 June 2002 and rates since 1 October 2002.
facts.F3: The 1st Defendant vacated and deserted the premises without the consent or permission of the Plaintiff on 12 October 2002.
facts.F4: The 1st Defendant returned keys of the premises to the Plaintiff on 1 November 2002.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff recovered possession of the premises on 11 December 2002 after giving due notice to the 1st and 2nd Defendants.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff instituted the proceedings against the 1st and 2nd Defendants on 11 June 2003.
facts.F7: The 2nd Defendant filed no defence against the Plaintiff’s claim.
facts.F8: Final and Interlocutory Judgment was entered against the 2nd Defendant on 25 November 2004 for a liquidated sum and for damages for breach of the Lease to be assessed.
facts.F9: The Plaintiff tried to re-let the premises and eventually succeeded in letting out the premises by late March 2003.
facts.F10: The Plaintiff entered into a new lease agreement with Cityray Technology (China) Limited for the premises for a term of 2 years commencing from 28 March 2003 at a monthly rent of $22,765 with a rent-free period between 28 March 2003 and 27 April 2003.
facts.F11: The Plaintiff suffered loss of rental between 11 December 2002 and 15 July 2003.
facts.F12: The rent of $22,765 at which the premises was let to Cityray was the market rent that could be reasonably obtained at that time.

reference_issues: Whether the Plaintiff is entitled to recover damages for breach of the Lease.
Whether the 2nd Defendant is liable as the guarantor under the Lease.
Whether the settlement agreement between the Plaintiff and the 2nd Defendant is valid and effective.

claim: Against conviction of one charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm
requested_remedy: Against conviction of one charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm

facts.F1: The appellant, Yung Pui Kit, was convicted by Magistrate Stephen Smout on 30 October 2003 of one charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.
facts.F2: The appellant was sentenced to a fine of $3,500.
facts.F3: The appellant and the victim, a woman, are neighbours and have a history of animosity.
facts.F4: On 26 April 2003, the woman was taking exercise near a jogging path in Junction Road Park, Kowloon City.
facts.F5: The woman testified that as she stretched out her arms, the fingers of her right hand touched the left forearm of a passing jogger, the appellant.
facts.F6: The woman said the appellant responded by punching her on the left eye with his right fist.
facts.F7: A passer-by, Mr Wong, heard the woman cry for help and approached the scene.
facts.F8: The woman was later found to have a bruise and swelling over the left eye.
facts.F9: The appellant testified that he was jogging when the woman punched him in the left side of the chest.
facts.F10: The appellant said the woman scratched him and he used both arms to ward her off.
facts.F11: Scratch marks were visible on the appellant's right forearm, and a medical report noted tenderness over the left chest wall.
facts.F12: The woman denied scratching the appellant, but the magistrate found the scratches may have been sustained during an attempt to prevent the use of her telephone.
facts.F13: The magistrate warned himself that the victim might have her own purposes to serve in testifying as she did.
facts.F14: The victim was found to be a witness of truth by the magistrate.

reference_issues: Whether the evidence of the victim was inherently implausible.
Whether the magistrate failed to fully consider the inconsistency of the denial by the victim of scratching the appellant and the scratch to the forearm of the appellant.
Whether the magistrate failed to fully consider the discrepancy between the evidence of the victim and that of Mr Wong as to whether a struggle took place between Mr Wong and the appellant.
Whether the magistrate failed to consider the account of the appellant was more consistent with the evidence of Mr Wong than that of the victim.
Whether the magistrate's findings in respect of the scratch to the arm of the appellant and the contusion to the wall of the chest of the appellant were wrong.
relevant_cases: R. v. Low [1961] HKLR 13

claim: common assault
requested_remedy: common assault
parties: Defendant: WONG Ping-nam, LAW Chak-fu, and CHING Kam-hung

facts.F1: The appellants were employees of the New Territories Urban Services Department.
facts.F2: They were part of a team that arrived at the Pak Kok Temporary Housing Estate in Tuen Mun on September 22, 1983, to carry out hawker clearance duties.
facts.F3: Hawkers fled, and goods were seized.
facts.F4: TONG Kai-hung, the complainant, threw at least one stone at the Urban Services Department vehicle and yelled abuse at the team.
facts.F5: The majority of the team members, including the first appellant, alighted from their vehicle and moved towards the complainant.
facts.F6: An altercation took place between the complainant and the first appellant, followed by an attack on the complainant by 7-8 team members, including the three appellants.
facts.F7: The complainant and his wife identified all three appellants as being among the attackers.
facts.F8: PW2 TAM Yat-on identified the second and third appellants as two of the men who assaulted the complainant.
facts.F9: PW3 KEUNG Yee-kin testified that the three appellants took part in the fight.
facts.F10: PW6 LEUNG Yee-tai gave clear evidence that a team of Urban Services Department officers assaulted the complainant, although he did not identify any appellants.
facts.F11: The learned magistrate had the opportunity to observe the demeanour of the witnesses and was in a better position to decide who was truthful and reliable.
facts.F12: The evidence of PW3 and PW6, independent witnesses who attempted to restrain the Urban Services Department team, corroborated the evidence of the complainant and his wife.
facts.F13: The medical report was considered to conclude that the force used was excessive.
facts.F14: The Urban Services Department team was pursuing a common object and everyone was ready to assist each other if necessary.

reference_issues: Whether there was sufficient evidence to support the conviction of the three appellants for common assault.
Whether the learned magistrate correctly approached the issue of guilt or innocence on the basis of common intention.
Whether the learned magistrate applied the proper standard of proof in reaching his decision.
relevant_cases: CHAN Wing-yuen v. The Queen (1977) H.K.L.R. 186

claim: The plaintiff claimed that Ma Weinan was liable for $11 million plus interest due under a guarantee dated 27 November 1997 apparently signed by Ma in support of facilities granted by the Bank to Horizon Engineering Services Limited.
requested_remedy: The plaintiff claimed that Ma Weinan was liable for $11 million plus interest due under a guarantee dated 27 November 1997 apparently signed by Ma in support of facilities granted by the Bank to Horizon Engineering Services Limited.
parties: Plaintiff: BANK OF CHINA (HONG KONG) LIMITED (formally known as THE CHINA AND SOUTH SEA BANK, LIMITED, HONG KONG BRANCH)

facts.F1: On 16 July 2001 the Bank obtained summary judgment against Ma for $11 million plus interest.
facts.F2: The judgment was based on a guarantee dated 27 November 1997 apparently signed by Ma in support of facilities granted by the Bank to Horizon.
facts.F3: Ma claims that he never signed the guarantee on which the judgment was based.
facts.F4: Ma was in Mainland China between January 1999 and December 2001 and could not be contacted.
facts.F5: BLC filed an Acknowledgment of Service as 'Solicitors for the 3rd Defendant' on 30 March 2000.
facts.F6: BLC filed a Defence, ostensibly on Ma's behalf, on 18 May 2000.
facts.F7: On 13 July 2001 BLC applied to cease acting for Ma.
facts.F8: On 16 July 2001 Master Kwan refused BLC's invitation to hear the application to cease to act at the same time as the Order 14 summons.
facts.F9: On 16 July 2001 the Court gave BLC leave to cease acting for Ma.
facts.F10: BLC never informed Ma that the Bank had obtained summary judgment.
facts.F11: Ma denies ever having instructed BLC to act for him.
facts.F12: Ma claims that service of the writ on him, by post at a Hong Kong address, was irregular.
facts.F13: Ma purchased the Sceneway Garden flat for $3.35 million on 27 December 2003.
facts.F14: Master Kwan granted a charging order nisi over the flat on 21 September 2004.
facts.F15: Ma's secretary noticed the envelope containing the copy order and informed Ma, who then applied to set aside Master Kwan's judgment and prevent the charging order from becoming absolute.
facts.F16: The court considered whether Ma should be granted leave to appeal out of time against Master Kwan's summary judgment, which had been made eight years prior, and found it to be just despite the time elapsed.
facts.F17: Ma's appeal against the summary judgment is to decide the genuineness of his signature on the guarantee.
facts.F18: The court held that service by posting to a Hong Kong address was not valid service on Ma while he was outside Hong Kong.

reference_issues: Whether Ma should be granted leave to appeal out of time against Master Kwan's summary judgment.
Whether Ma's appeal against the summary judgment should be allowed.
Whether judgment should be set aside in any event for bad service.
Whether the charging order should be set aside.
